title: Factorization of affine difference charts through a Cartesian tower
statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Use schemes, finite-type and separated morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], affine spaces and their coordinate functions [def-sbc-affine-space], and scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $f:U\to V$ and $g:V\to T$ be smooth separated finite-type maps of affine finite-type $k$-schemes of pure dimensions $d,e\geq0$, with specified etale charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ and $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$, having coordinate functions $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$ and $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_e)$. Put $B=U$, $Q=U\times_TV$, $W=U\times_TU$, $a(u,u')=(u,fu')$, $b(u,v)=u$, $s(u)=(u,fu)$ and $t(u)=(u,u)$. Write $P_r:\mathbf A_B^r\to B$, $z_r:B\to\mathbf A_B^r$, and $q:\mathbf A_B^{d+e}\to\mathbf A_B^e$ for the projection keeping the last $e$ coordinates [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. Define
$$G:Q\to\mathbf A_B^e,\quad(u,v)\mapsto(u,y(v)-y(fu)),$$
$$R=Q\times_{\mathbf A_B^e}\mathbf A_B^{d+e}=\mathbf A_Q^d,\quad q_Q:R\to Q,\quad J:R\to\mathbf A_B^{d+e},$$
$$H:W\to R,\quad(u,u')\mapsto((u,fu'),x(u')-x(u)),\qquad F=JH.$$

Then $a=q_QH$, $b=P_eG$, $qJ=Gq_Q$, $Gs=z_e$ and $Ft=z_{d+e}$. The map $F$ has the ordered coordinates $(x(u')-x(u),y(fu')-y(fu))$ over $B$. The maps $G,H,J,F$ are etale, separated and finite type; all displayed schemes are affine. More precisely, $G$ is the base change of the chart of $g$ followed by translation by $-y(fu)$, $H$ is the base change of the chart of $f$ followed by translation by $-x(u)$, and $J$ is the base change of $G$.
The square defining $R$ is Cartesian. Independently, $q$ is the base change of $P_d:\mathbf A_B^d\to B$ along $P_e$, via the projection $\mathbf A_B^{d+e}\to\mathbf A_B^d$. Thus $q,P_e,P_eq,q_Q$ are smooth of relative dimensions $d,e,d+e,d$. If $W_f=U\times_VU$ and $H_f:W_f\to\mathbf A_B^d$ sends $(u,u')$ to $(u,x(u')-x(u))$, the square with horizontal maps $H_f,H$ and vertical maps $W_f\to W$ and $\mathbf A_B^d\to R$ induced by $s:B\to Q$ is Cartesian. The analogous square of $G_g:V\times_TV\to\mathbf A_V^e$, $(v,v')\mapsto(v,y(v')-y(v))$, and $G$ is Cartesian over $f:B\to V$. In particular $H_f,G_g$ are etale and carry the respective diagonals to zero sections. These assertions hold for empty affine schemes and for $d=0$ or $e=0$, with empty coordinate blocks. For any smooth separated finite-type pair $f_0:X\to Y$, $g_0:Y\to Z$ of pure dimensions $d,e$ between finite-type $k$-schemes and any $x\in X$, there are affine open neighbourhoods $U$ of $x$, $V$ of $f_0(x)$, $T$ of $g_0f_0(x)$ with $f_0(U)\subseteq V$, $g_0(V)\subseteq T$ and compatible etale charts of the above form for the restricted pair.

proof.text: Use AffineSpace.hom_ext to prove directly the universal property of the ordered first and last coordinate blocks. The lift of maps into the two blocks concatenates their global coordinate sections using Fin.addCases. Equality of the two base morphisms gives its structure morphism. Coordinate extensionality proves both projection equations and uniqueness. Translation by a tuple v has inverse translation by -v, by AffineSpace.translation_add and translation_zero. These are the constructions of [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Step 1: standard coordinates; polynomial translations and ordered affine product

proof.text: Use [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product] to identify R with affine d-space over Q by its stated explicit construction. The first projection of J is the affine-space base-change map along Q to U; its last projection is G composed with the structure morphism of R. Pasting with the ordered affine-product square from Step 1 proves that the square (J,q_Q,q,G) is Cartesian. Affineness of Q, W, the self-products and the affine spaces follows from the standard Mathlib affine-pullback and affine-space instances, expressing [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

source.place: Step 1: canonical Cartesian product identifications; explicit description of R

proof.text: Write $c_g:V\to\mathbf A_T^e$ for the given chart. Base change along $gf:B\to T$ gives $Q\to\mathbf A_B^e$, $(u,v)\mapsto(u,y(v))$. Compose it with the automorphism from Step 1 having translation tuple $-y(fu)$; the result is exactly $G$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] the base-changed chart is etale; its use only requires that $c_g$ is etale. An automorphism is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion], hence etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Clause (2) of that node makes $G$ etale.

source.place: Tags 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale); polynomial translation as in blueprint Step 1

proof.text: The square (a,second projection of W,second projection of Q,f) is Cartesian by cancelling the Cartesian square defining Q from the square defining W, using IsPullback.of_right. For any Cartesian square and chart c with c followed by projection equal to the original morphism, AffineSpace.hom_ext identifies its base-changed chart with homOfVector of the top projection and the pulled-back coordinates; cancelling AffineSpace.isPullback_map proves that this chart square is Cartesian. Apply this to obtain Hraw. The coordinate calculation identifies H with Hraw followed by translation by the negative first coordinates. Base change and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] prove H etale. The square of J from Step 2 proves J etale as a base change of G, and F=H followed by J is etale. The base squares use [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Step 1: translated f-chart, base-changed G-chart, and composite difference chart

proof.text: Substitute the formula for $H$ into that for $J$ from Step 2. This gives $F(u,u')=(u,x(u')-x(u),y(fu')-y(fu))$, with the first block before the last block. Projection now gives $q_QH=a$, $P_eG=b$ and $qJ=Gq_Q$. On the graph $s(u)=(u,fu)$ the last differences vanish, giving $Gs=z_e$. On $t(u)=(u,u)$ both blocks vanish, giving $Ft=z_{d+e}$. These are equalities of scheme maps: on every affine coordinate ring they fix the base ring and have the displayed identical images of each polynomial generator, not merely identical values on ordinary points.

source.place: Step 1: ordered coordinate and section identities

proof.text: Every displayed scheme is affine by Step 2. Mathlib gives IsSeparated for any morphism with affine source ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]) and IsAffineHom for any map between affine schemes; the latter gives QuasiCompact, as also expressed by the affine source and quasi-separated target criterion [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. An etale map is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], hence locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply these instances to G,H,J,F; no claim that arbitrary etale maps are quasi-compact is needed.

source.place: Tag 01KU, separated permanence; morphisms.tex Tags 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), 01TS (finite presentation), applied only to maps between affine schemes

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], $P_d,P_e,P_{d+e}$ are smooth of relative dimensions $d,e,d+e$. Step 1 identifies $q$ as the base change of $P_d$ along $P_e$; [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] (1) therefore gives dimension $d$ for $q$. Step 2 identifies $q_Q$ with the projection $\mathbf A_Q^d\to Q$, so the affine-space lemma gives dimension $d$ for it. Finally $P_eq=P_{d+e}$ by the base coordinate projection. This proves all the asserted smoothness and dimension statements.

Prove first the Cartesian square (i,first projection,a,s) of [def-pc-fibre-product] directly: a test pair in W and U has first component the given U point and second component with the same f-image; its lift to the self-product over V is forced by these two components. Coordinate extensionality proves that H composed with i equals differenceFirst composed with includeR. Cancel the affine-space base-change square along s from the pasted square to obtain the asserted restriction square. Independently base-change the chart cf along f and translate by its negative coordinates; this proves differenceFirst etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The diagonal coordinates are differences of equal sections and hence zero.

source.place: Step 1: Cartesian restriction of the f difference chart along the graph s

proof.text: Cancel the square defining the self-product of g from the square defining Q to obtain the Cartesian square (j,first projection,first projection,f) of [def-pc-fibre-product]. The two composites of its difference charts into affine e-space over V agree by coordinate extensionality using [def-sbc-affine-space]. Cancel the affine-space base-change square over f to obtain the required restriction square. The general base-changed-chart and translation proof from Step 8, applied to cg, proves differenceFirst of g etale using [def-weil-open-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Its diagonal coordinates vanish.

source.place: Step 1: Cartesian restriction of the g difference chart over f

proof.text: Apply the source-library theorem Smooth.exists_etale_to_affineSpace to g at f(x), with its given relative dimension e; this is the prescribed-dimension version of [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]. For f take a standard smooth affine presentation of its given relative dimension d. Use Mathlib exists_basicOpen_le_appLE_of_appLE_of_isAffine to refine this presentation to a basic affine neighbourhood V inside the chosen domain of the g chart, and to a basic affine neighbourhood U of x. Apply the source-library exists_etale_to_affineSpace_of_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension to this refined presentation for cf. Restrict cg by the open immersion V into its original domain; it stays etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The structure-map identity follows from map_resLE. The restrictions of f and g keep their given relative dimensions by the source-open and target-open permanence of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Local finite type of the restrictions and of their maps to Spec k follows from the restriction and composition instances for [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. All sources are affine: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] gives separatedness; maps to affine targets are affine and hence quasi-compact, as in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Thus all required finite-type assertions hold, without any extra affineness or separatedness hypothesis on X,Y,Z.

If $d=0$ or $e=0$, omit the corresponding polynomial generators; translation is the identity on that empty block, and $\mathbf A_B^0=B$ by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Every construction and inverse in Steps 1-9 still applies. If an affine scheme is empty its coordinate ring is the zero ring; the polynomial substitutions and tensor-product identifications still hold, and the universal properties still quantify over supplied maps, so no nonempty point is required. The final local-existence assertion is quantified over $x\in X$ and is vacuous when $X$ is empty. Thus these edge cases require no additional hypotheses.
